rationale: The workflow already implements the dependency-cache optimization that P-LIT-GHA-CACHE/P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE describe: every job that installs dependencies uses astral-sh/setup-uv with enable-cache (default true; the release job explicitly disables it for a clean build), which persists uv's download/wheel cache through the Actions cache. Adding a separate actions/cache step would be redundant and is contraindicated by the pattern ('An equivalent cache already exists'); moreover the repository is uv-based (pyproject.toml plus uv.lock), whereas the matching experiment added cache to a pip-based workflow. P-LIT-FAIL-FAST is contraindicated because every Python matrix result is required by the coverage gate (the coverage job fails unless all test jobs succeed and coverage is 100%). P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE is already provided through concurrency.cancel-in-progress. No Bazel/Go/Maven build exists, there are no scheduled workflows, and test selection/skipping is contraindicated by the full-coverage contract. No supported, safe, minimal workflow change remains.
